name: COURCHEVEL
description: Courchevel is an Omaha poker variant popular in France and the UK. Each player receives five hole cards and one community card is dealt face up before the first betting round. After that round, two more board cards complete the flop; then turn and river with betting after each. Players must use exactly two of their five hole cards with three board cards to make the best hand. Best hand wins the pot.

content.text: Courchevel is an Omaha poker variant popular in France and the UK. Each player receives five hole cards and one community card is dealt face up before the first betting round. After that round, two more board cards complete the flop; then turn and river with betting after each. Players must use exactly two of their five hole cards with three board cards to make the best hand. Best hand wins the pot.

Country/Region of Origin: France
Time Period: Late 20th century
Historical Development: Named after the Courchevel ski resort in the French Alps; reportedly invented by tourists. Commonly played at the Aviation Club de France in Paris (now closed).
Cultural Significance: Popular in France; spread to UK and other parts of Europe.
Type: Standard 52-card deck. One deck. No jokers.

Five hole cards each, dealt face down. One community card dealt face up before the first betting round. After that round, dealer burns one card and deals two more face up (three-card flop). Then turn (one card) and river (one card), with a burn before each. Betting after each street.

items.text: Courchevel High: Standard version; only the best high hand wins the pot. Pot Limit or other limits.
Courchevel Hi-Low 8-or-Better: Pot splits between best high and best qualifying low (8-high or better); each hand uses exactly two hole and three board. Available in some venues.
